meta.title: Motivation, Exposure & Acquisition
meta.randomizationRule: Randomize question selection/order and answer-option order on every attempt; never reuse an exact attempt signature.
meta.alignment: TKT Module 1 — Background to language learning: motivation; exposure to language and focus on form; acquisition; silent period; interaction

questions.prompt: A learner studies English because she wants a better job. Which factor is most directly involved?
questions.correctAnswer: Motivation
questions.explanation: Motivation concerns the reasons and willingness a learner has for learning.

questions.prompt: Which classroom choice is most likely to increase motivation?
options: Giving only repetitive tasks unrelated to learners' goals
questions.correctAnswer: Using relevant, achievable tasks
questions.explanation: Relevant and achievable work can help learners see value and experience success.

questions.prompt: A learner becomes more willing to participate after receiving encouraging feedback. What has most likely increased?
questions.correctAnswer: Motivation
questions.explanation: Positive feedback can strengthen confidence and willingness to engage.

questions.prompt: Why is motivation important in language learning?
options: It can influence effort, persistence and engagement
It determines a learner's first language
It replaces the need for exposure
questions.correctAnswer: It can influence effort, persistence and engagement
questions.explanation: Motivation affects how much effort learners invest and how long they persist.

questions.prompt: Which teacher action is most likely to support motivation in a mixed-ability class?
options: Set challenging but achievable goals and recognise progress
Use the same difficult task for everyone without support
questions.correctAnswer: Set challenging but achievable goals and recognise progress
questions.explanation: Appropriate challenge and visible progress can support motivation.

questions.prompt: A learner attends optional English practice every week because she enjoys communicating with classmates. What is the clearest explanation?
options: She is in a silent period
questions.correctAnswer: She is motivated to learn
questions.explanation: Voluntary participation and enjoyment are signs of motivation.

questions.prompt: Which factor can most directly reduce learner motivation?
options: Repeated failure with no sense of progress
questions.correctAnswer: Repeated failure with no sense of progress
questions.explanation: Persistent failure without support can reduce confidence and willingness to continue.

questions.prompt: Which statement about motivation is most accurate?
options: It can change over time and be influenced by classroom experience
It is fixed and cannot be influenced by teaching
It matters only at beginner level
questions.correctAnswer: It can change over time and be influenced by classroom experience
questions.explanation: Motivation is dynamic and can change with experience, goals and classroom conditions.

questions.prompt: A teacher lets learners choose between two project topics connected to their interests. What is the most likely purpose?
questions.correctAnswer: Increase motivation
questions.explanation: Choice and personal relevance can increase learner involvement.

questions.prompt: Which situation best shows motivation affecting learning behaviour?
options: A learner practises regularly because passing an exam is an important goal
A learner hears English on television by chance
A learner notices a verb ending
questions.correctAnswer: A learner practises regularly because passing an exam is an important goal
questions.explanation: The goal is driving sustained learning effort.

questions.prompt: A learner regularly hears and reads English outside class. Which concept does this illustrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Exposure
questions.explanation: Exposure means coming into contact with the target language.

questions.prompt: Which activity provides learners with exposure to English?
options: Listening to a podcast in English
Studying only translations with no English examples
questions.correctAnswer: Listening to a podcast in English
questions.explanation: Listening to English gives learners direct contact with target-language input.

questions.prompt: Why is rich exposure useful for language learning?
options: It gives learners many examples of how language is used
It removes the need to communicate
questions.correctAnswer: It gives learners many examples of how language is used
questions.explanation: Frequent input helps learners notice patterns, meanings and usage.

questions.prompt: Which source can provide authentic exposure?
options: A real-world video made for English-speaking viewers
A list of grammar labels only
A translation test with no target-language input
questions.correctAnswer: A real-world video made for English-speaking viewers
questions.explanation: Authentic audio or video can expose learners to naturally occurring language.

questions.prompt: Which statement about exposure is most accurate?
options: Exposure is important, but interaction and focus on form can also support learning
Exposure means learners should never study form
questions.correctAnswer: Exposure is important, but interaction and focus on form can also support learning
questions.explanation: Interaction and focus on form can complement exposure.

questions.prompt: A teacher increases the amount of English learners hear during classroom routines. What factor is being increased?
questions.correctAnswer: Exposure
questions.explanation: Learners are receiving more target-language input.

questions.prompt: Which situation gives the greatest amount of direct exposure to English?
options: Reading articles and listening to English every day
Studying only explanations in another language
questions.correctAnswer: Reading articles and listening to English every day
questions.explanation: Regular contact with the target language increases exposure.

questions.prompt: Why might exposure without meaningful engagement be insufficient?
options: Learners also benefit from interaction and attention to useful forms
Exposure is relevant only to pronunciation
questions.correctAnswer: Learners also benefit from interaction and attention to useful forms
questions.explanation: Input is important, but learning is strengthened when learners process and use language.

questions.prompt: Which teacher choice increases exposure most directly?
options: Use English for understandable classroom instructions and routines
Translate every instruction before using English
questions.correctAnswer: Use English for understandable classroom instructions and routines
questions.explanation: Comprehensible target-language routines increase input.

questions.prompt: A learner watches many English videos but rarely tries to understand or use the language. Which statement is best?
options: The learner has exposure, but other learning processes may still be needed
questions.correctAnswer: The learner has exposure, but other learning processes may still be needed
questions.explanation: Contact with English is exposure, but interaction and purposeful processing can still matter.

questions.prompt: A learner gradually begins using a phrase after hearing it repeatedly in meaningful situations, without studying a rule. Which process is this?
questions.correctAnswer: Acquisition
questions.explanation: Acquisition can develop through meaningful exposure and use without explicit rule study.

questions.prompt: Which situation best illustrates acquisition?
options: Picking up a phrase after repeated meaningful exposure
questions.correctAnswer: Picking up a phrase after repeated meaningful exposure
questions.explanation: Acquisition develops gradually through meaningful contact with language.

questions.prompt: Which feature is most closely associated with acquisition?
options: Language develops gradually through exposure and use
Every rule must be memorised first
questions.correctAnswer: Language develops gradually through exposure and use
questions.explanation: Acquisition is generally gradual.

questions.prompt: Why is meaningful input important for acquisition?
options: Learners need language they can process and connect with meaning
questions.correctAnswer: Learners need language they can process and connect with meaning
questions.explanation: Acquisition is supported by understandable language used meaningfully.

questions.prompt: Which statement best distinguishes acquisition from explicit study?
options: Acquisition can develop implicitly through exposure and use; explicit study involves conscious attention to rules
questions.correctAnswer: Acquisition can develop implicitly through exposure and use; explicit study involves conscious attention to rules
questions.explanation: Acquisition is often associated with implicit development.

questions.prompt: A learner starts producing a pattern correctly before being able to explain the rule. What may this illustrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Acquisition
questions.explanation: Implicit knowledge can develop before a learner can verbalise a rule.

questions.prompt: Which classroom condition is most supportive of acquisition?
options: Frequent meaningful exposure and opportunities to use language
questions.correctAnswer: Frequent meaningful exposure and opportunities to use language
questions.explanation: Acquisition is supported by rich input and meaningful use.

questions.prompt: Which statement about acquisition is most accurate?
options: It can occur gradually without full conscious awareness of every rule
questions.correctAnswer: It can occur gradually without full conscious awareness of every rule
questions.explanation: Acquisition may be gradual and implicit.

questions.prompt: A learner understands a new expression after repeatedly hearing it in real conversations. Which concept is most relevant?
questions.correctAnswer: Acquisition
questions.explanation: Repeated meaningful exposure can support gradual acquisition.

questions.prompt: Which example is least characteristic of acquisition?
options: Memorising a metalanguage definition without using the target language
Picking up a phrase from repeated meaningful exposure
Developing a feel for what sounds natural
questions.correctAnswer: Memorising a metalanguage definition without using the target language
questions.explanation: This is explicit study rather than implicit language acquisition.

questions.prompt: A beginner listens carefully for several weeks but says very little at first. Which concept may explain this?
questions.correctAnswer: Silent period
questions.explanation: A silent period is a stage when learners may process language before producing much of it.

questions.prompt: During a silent period, a learner may:
options: Listen and build understanding before speaking much
questions.correctAnswer: Listen and build understanding before speaking much
questions.explanation: Low production does not necessarily mean no learning is taking place.

questions.prompt: What should a teacher generally avoid doing with a learner in a silent period?
questions.correctAnswer: Forcing immediate extended production
questions.explanation: Pressure to speak before a learner is ready may not support learning.

questions.prompt: Which teacher response is most appropriate for a learner who understands instructions but is not yet ready to speak much?
options: Provide input and allow low-pressure responses
Assume the learner has learned nothing
questions.correctAnswer: Provide input and allow low-pressure responses
questions.explanation: Learners may benefit from continued exposure without pressure.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the silent period is most accurate?
options: Limited speaking can coexist with active language processing
It means the learner is unmotivated
questions.correctAnswer: Limited speaking can coexist with active language processing
questions.explanation: Learners can build receptive knowledge before extensive production.

questions.prompt: A new learner points to correct pictures and follows instructions but rarely speaks. What concept is most relevant?
questions.correctAnswer: Silent period
questions.explanation: The learner shows comprehension despite limited oral production.

questions.prompt: Which activity is most suitable during a silent period?
options: Listen and choose the correct picture
questions.correctAnswer: Listen and choose the correct picture
questions.explanation: Low-pressure response tasks allow participation without forcing extended speech.

questions.prompt: Why should a teacher not automatically interpret silence as lack of learning?
options: Learners may be developing comprehension before production
questions.correctAnswer: Learners may be developing comprehension before production
questions.explanation: Receptive knowledge can develop before extensive output.

questions.prompt: What is the teacher's most supportive role during a silent period?
options: Continue providing understandable language and low-pressure participation
questions.correctAnswer: Continue providing understandable language and low-pressure participation
questions.explanation: Rich input and supportive participation can help learners progress.

questions.prompt: Which statement is least appropriate?
options: A learner in a silent period should be forced to speak extensively from day one
A learner may understand more than they can produce
questions.correctAnswer: A learner in a silent period should be forced to speak extensively from day one
questions.explanation: The silent period is better supported through input and low-pressure participation.

questions.prompt: Two learners ask and answer questions to complete an information-gap task. Which factor is being promoted?
questions.correctAnswer: Interaction
questions.explanation: Interaction occurs when learners exchange meaning with other people.

questions.prompt: Why is interaction useful for language learning?
options: It gives learners opportunities to understand, respond and negotiate meaning
It removes the need for exposure
questions.correctAnswer: It gives learners opportunities to understand, respond and negotiate meaning
questions.explanation: Interaction requires learners to process language and respond meaningfully.

questions.prompt: A learner says, “Sorry, what do you mean?” during pair work. Which process is this part of?
questions.correctAnswer: Interaction and negotiation of meaning
questions.explanation: Clarification requests help learners negotiate understanding.

questions.prompt: Which activity creates the strongest need for genuine interaction?
options: An information-gap task in which partners have different information
Copying a sentence from the board
questions.correctAnswer: An information-gap task in which partners have different information
questions.explanation: Learners need to communicate to complete the task.

questions.prompt: How can interaction complement exposure?
options: It gives learners opportunities to process and use the language they encounter
It replaces all need for input
It prevents learners from noticing form
questions.correctAnswer: It gives learners opportunities to process and use the language they encounter
questions.explanation: Exposure provides input; interaction adds active communication.

questions.prompt: Which classroom activity most clearly promotes interaction?
questions.correctAnswer: A pair-work problem-solving task
questions.explanation: Learners need to exchange ideas and respond to one another.

questions.prompt: A learner modifies a sentence after a partner says, “I don't understand.” What is happening?
questions.correctAnswer: Negotiation of meaning during interaction
questions.explanation: The learner adjusts language to make meaning clearer.

questions.prompt: Which statement about interaction is most accurate?
options: It can help learners notice gaps in their ability to express meaning
It is useful only for advanced learners
It means learners should never receive teacher input
questions.correctAnswer: It can help learners notice gaps in their ability to express meaning
questions.explanation: Attempting to communicate can reveal what learners cannot yet express.

questions.prompt: Why are pair and group tasks often useful for interaction?
options: They increase opportunities for learners to exchange language
questions.correctAnswer: They increase opportunities for learners to exchange language
questions.explanation: Pair and group formats can increase learner participation.

questions.prompt: Which activity provides exposure but very little interaction?
options: Watching a video without any response or discussion
questions.correctAnswer: Watching a video without any response or discussion
questions.explanation: The learner receives input, but there is little or no exchange of meaning.

questions.prompt: During a communicative activity, the teacher briefly draws attention to the past tense ending -ed. Which concept is this?
questions.correctAnswer: Focus on form
questions.explanation: Focus on form draws attention to language features within meaningful language use.

questions.prompt: Which classroom action best illustrates focus on form?
options: Briefly noticing a grammar or pronunciation feature during meaningful communication
Avoiding all attention to language form
questions.correctAnswer: Briefly noticing a grammar or pronunciation feature during meaningful communication
questions.explanation: Focus on form connects language features with communicative context.

questions.prompt: Why can focus on form complement exposure?
options: Learners may benefit from noticing important language features in the input
Focus on form means translating everything
questions.correctAnswer: Learners may benefit from noticing important language features in the input
questions.explanation: Attention to form can help learners detect useful patterns.

questions.prompt: A learner repeatedly says “He go to work.” The teacher briefly highlights third-person -s and then returns to the task. What is this?
questions.correctAnswer: Focus on form
questions.explanation: The teacher momentarily directs attention to a relevant grammatical feature.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes focus on form?
options: Attention to particular language features can occur within meaning-focused activity
It means teaching isolated grammar with no context in every lesson
questions.correctAnswer: Attention to particular language features can occur within meaning-focused activity
questions.explanation: Focus on form can be integrated into communicative work.

questions.prompt: Which teacher move is the clearest example of focus on form?
options: Pause pair work briefly to clarify a useful structure learners are struggling with
Cancel all communication and teach terminology for the whole lesson
questions.correctAnswer: Pause pair work briefly to clarify a useful structure learners are struggling with
questions.explanation: The teacher responds to a language need arising during meaningful activity.

questions.prompt: What is a likely benefit of focus on form?
options: It can help learners notice the relationship between form and meaning/use
It removes the need for exposure
questions.correctAnswer: It can help learners notice the relationship between form and meaning/use
questions.explanation: Attention to form can make language patterns more noticeable.

questions.prompt: Which situation best combines exposure, interaction and focus on form?
options: Learners listen to a model, discuss a task in pairs, and briefly analyse a useful language pattern
Learners silently copy a rule only
Learners watch a video with no follow-up
questions.correctAnswer: Learners listen to a model, discuss a task in pairs, and briefly analyse a useful language pattern
questions.explanation: This combines input, meaningful communication and attention to form.

questions.prompt: A teacher underlines recurring language in a text and asks learners what pattern they notice. Which concept is most relevant?
questions.correctAnswer: Focus on form
questions.explanation: The task directs attention to a language pattern in meaningful input.

questions.prompt: Which statement is least accurate?
options: Focus on form means meaningful communication must stop completely whenever grammar is discussed
Focus on form can be brief and responsive to learner needs
Focus on form can help learners notice features in input
questions.correctAnswer: Focus on form means meaningful communication must stop completely whenever grammar is discussed
questions.explanation: Focus on form can be integrated into communication rather than replacing it.

items.example: A learner studies because passing an exam is an important personal goal.
A learner regularly listens to English podcasts.
A learner gradually begins using a phrase after hearing it many times.
A beginner understands instructions but says very little at first.
Learners exchange information to complete a task.
The teacher briefly highlights a grammatical feature during a communicative activity.

matchingSets.instruction: Match each description with the correct term.

items.example: Gradual development of language through meaningful input and use.
A phase of limited production despite developing comprehension.
Exchange of meaning between learners or speakers.
Attention to a language feature within meaning-focused activity.
